samples.question: This image shows one round gauge dial. The grey page frame, the four short grey corner ticks, the grey rim circle, the grey hub at the centre and the grey pointer are fixed decoration: the pointer's direction is sampled independently of everything else and never indicates the answer. The readings of the dial are the coloured dots printed just inside the rim. They form exactly five separate groups spaced around the rim, and the groups are always the same five sizes: one dot, two dots, three dots, four dots and five dots. A group is a run of dots that are close together, and the blank arc between two neighbouring groups is always wider than the gap between two dots of the same group. The five groups are arranged so that their sizes ascend steadily as you travel around the rim in one rotational direction, and descend as you travel the other way; which rotational direction that is changes from image to image, as do the dot colour, the dot size, the position of the groups around the rim, the dial's centre and radius, and the pointer. Judge the direction as it appears on the page, where clockwise runs from the top of the dial to its right side. Read the groups you can actually see in this image, and do not answer from the direction a dial or a clock face usually runs. Travelling around the rim from the one-dot group to the two-dot group to the three-dot group and on to the five-dot group, which way are you going? Answer clockwise or counterclockwise.
